text:
Anya: Anyone seeing gRPC connection resets between shards in the us-east1 GPU pool? pods showing short 502s and occasional Evicted events.
Mike: Yep, alert fired ~09:11 UTC. Nodes in gce-gpu-east-02 showing conntrack spikes.
Sunil: Can you share conntrack numbers?
Anya: On one node:
```
# cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
196608
# conntrack -L | wc -l
195421
# cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range
32768	60999
```
So table almost full and ephemeral ports getting chewed.
InfraBot: Auto-mitigation: +3 nodes added to gce-gpu-east-02, drain-protected during scale, oncall notified.
Kate: Are these cross-node pod egress flows hitting SNAT? If model workers don't use hostNetwork, we'll create SNAT entries for every flow.
Leo: kube-proxy logs show many SYN_RECV and retries. We're on ipvs but SNAT for egress still applies.
Anya: My hypothesis: many sub-100ms RPCs with aggressive client retries -> conntrack churn -> kernel starts dropping -> client libs backoff poorly -> amplification.
Mike: Traces show retry storms after the first packet drops. Throughput ~8-12k req/s for a 2m window. Node CPU and net queues spiked.
Sunil: Quick actions we can take now:
- bump net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max to 800k on a canary
- tighten nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_syn_sent / fin_wait to reduce stale rows
- expand ip_local_port_range upper bound
- encourage hostNetwork for latency-sensitive shard pods or use hostPort
Anya: I'm going to apply on a canary:
```
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=800000
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range=\"15000 65000\"
```
InfraBot: DaemonSet job launched to roll sysctl changes to GPU nodes (canary -> phased).
Kate: Longer term items:
- Node-local SNAT pools so each node has more ephemeral SNAT capacity
- Evaluate eBPF CNI (conntrack bypass/inlined socket) in staging
- Tune client libs: connection pooling + keepalive windows to avoid new TCP per request
- Consider hostNetwork or DSR for intra-cluster large model sharding traffic where security allows
Leo: Also discovered 2 nodes with MTU mismatch (1450 vs 1500) causing fragmentation/retries and extra conntrack state. Fixing MTU removed a bunch of retransmits on those hosts.
Sunil: Note about RDMA pods 12: some RDMA-enabled pods fall back to TCP on non-RDMA paths and create duplicate flow patterns; we should test fallback path in staging.
Anya: After canary bump, conntrack_count on canary settled and incoming reset errors stopped. Rolling the sysctl changes to rest of pool.
Mike: Filed incident doc + runbook: https://go/internal/incidents/1784 (contains queries, rollback, and alert thresholds). Alert updated to trigger at 65% nf_conntrack_max per node.
InfraBot: Incident severity set to SEV2. event_id: seve-2026-03-18-1784123456.
Kate: Quick cost FYI: scaling up nodes and sysctl roll will add ~5-7% spend for the pool window. Log on ROI vs failed requests.
Leo: I'll write a short playbook for high-conn workloads (keepalive, pooling, hostNetwork patterns, MTU checks).
oncall: watching overnight; will escalate if conntrack > 70% persists.
Anya: Thanks team. Keeping the sysctl change for 48h and we'll coordinate app-side fixes and CNI upgrade in the next sprint. :thumbsup:
